Chodov Fortress
A medieval fortress in the heart of modern Chodov.

Chodov's most distinctive historic landmark began as a medieval moated fortress. Today it is a cultural centre with exhibitions and concerts. Its circular layout and inner courtyard are particularly striking.
Explore the exterior and check the programme before visiting an exhibition. Admission depends on the event.
Gallery and ticket office Tue–Sun 13:00–19:00; closed Monday.
Depends on the exhibition or event; a single admission price has not been verified.
Kunratice Forest
Woodland paths and a peaceful escape near Chodov.
About 284 hectares of woodland offer natural paths, the Kunratice stream valley and the ruins of Nový hrad, associated with King Wenceslas IV. Choose a gentle walk or a longer outing.
Some paths are unpaved. Enter at your own risk. Educational stops do not form a continuously marked circular trail.
Open natural area without a ticket office.
Free admission.
Westfield Chodov
Shopping, restaurants and cinema under one roof.
A practical choice for shopping, a meal, cinema or a rainy-day programme. Individual businesses inside the shopping centre may keep different hours.
Check the opening hours of the particular restaurant, shop or cinema separately.
Shopping centre daily 9:00–21:00.
Entry to the centre is free; cinema and other services charge their own prices.
Jedenáctka VS
An indoor swimming and sports complex.
This indoor pool and sports complex suits individuals and families. Swimming pools, sports facilities and children's swimming areas have separate spaces.
Check restrictions on public swimming and the current admission price for the length of your visit.
Pool Mon–Fri 6:30–21:00; Sat–Sun and public holidays 8:00–21:00.
Indicative prices from CZK 160 adult / 120 reduced / 340 family according to Prague City Tourism; check the exact ticket type.
Toulcův dvůr
A historic farm, animals and nature for families.
The historic farm in Hostivař offers encounters with animals, nature and educational activities. It is especially suitable for families seeking a quieter day outside the centre.
The farm and nature area charge admission. Groups larger than 10 have special visiting and booking rules.
Jan–Feb and Nov–Dec 10:00–16:00; Mar–Jun and Sep–Oct 10:00–18:00; Jul–Aug 9:00–18:00.
Farm and nature area: adults CZK 60; children from 3, seniors and disability card holders CZK 30; family CZK 130.
Hostivař Reservoir
A waterside walk surrounded by green parkland.
Walk beside the water near Hostivař Forest Park. In summer, the managed beach is a separate paid service; distinguish the beach from the public paths.
The beach is seasonal and swimming depends on operation and water quality. Public woodland and the paid beach are different areas.
Public paths have no set visiting hours; check the official website for seasonal beach operation.

Public paths free. When open: full-day beach CZK 170 adult; seniors, disability card holders and children under 140 cm CZK 110; under 100 cm free. The official website lists the beaches as closed on 8 October 2026.
Průhonice Park
A UNESCO-listed landscape park around a château.
Romantic paths, ponds and botanical scenery surround Průhonice Château. Allow half a day, especially during rhododendron flowering or autumn colours.
This is not a short walk from the hotel. Take public transport or a taxi to the park, then explore on foot. Tickets are also checked inside.
Daily: Jan–Feb and Nov–Dec 8:00–17:00; Mar 7:00–18:00; Apr and Oct 7:00–19:00; May–Sep 7:00–20:00.
Adults CZK 160; reduced CZK 110; family CZK 430; dog CZK 50.
Průhonice Dendrological Garden
Seasonal flowers, trees and beautiful garden compositions.
The garden specialises in collections of trees, shrubs, perennials and landscape design. A pleasant option for plant lovers and families, with highlights changing through the seasons.
The 2026 season ends on 8 November. Last admission is one hour before closing.
Season approximately March–8 November. Apr and Oct Tue–Sun 9:00–18:00; May–Aug Tue–Sun 9:00–19:00; Sep Tue–Sun 9:00–18:00; 1–8 Nov 9:00–17:00.
Adults CZK 150; reduced CZK 100; family CZK 350.
Aquapalace Praha
Water slides, pools and relaxation in Čestlice.
Water World offers slides, pools, a wild river and family attractions. It makes a full-day programme in bad weather. Sauna and wellness access may cost extra.
Water World tickets differ from combined Sauna + Water World tickets. Prices vary by day and online purchase.
Water World Mon–Wed 10:00–20:00; Thu–Fri 10:00–22:00; Sat 9:00–22:00; Sun 9:00–20:00, except special dates.
Water World only: adults Mon–Thu 3 hours CZK 1,049 / day CZK 1,149; Fri–Sun and public holidays 3 hours CZK 1,299 / day CZK 1,399.
Hamerský Pond and HAMR Záběhlice
Waterside views with sports facilities nearby.
Záběhlice combines a walk beside the pond with tennis, squash or a restaurant stop. It is a quieter urban outing with optional sports.
The public pond walk is separate from paid sports facilities. Book sports according to the operator's rules.
Public pond paths freely accessible; HAMR sports complex daily 7:00–23:00.
Public walk free; sports and food according to the operator's current price list.
Prague Castle
Royal history and magnificent views above the Vltava.
Explore the extensive historic grounds with St Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St George's Basilica and Golden Lane. Courtyards are accessible separately from ticketed interiors.
Walking through the grounds and entering buildings are different activities. Security checks and exceptional closures may apply.
Grounds daily 6:00–22:00; visitor buildings Apr–Oct 9:00–17:00, Nov–Mar 9:00–16:00.
Main circuit CZK 450; reduced CZK 300; family CZK 950. Public access through the grounds does not require this ticket.
Charles Bridge
A Gothic stone bridge with views towards the castle.
The statue-lined bridge crosses the Vltava between the Old Town and Malá Strana. Early morning and evening offer a special atmosphere and views of towers and riverside buildings.
Crossing the bridge is free. The neighbouring bridge towers charge separate admission.
Public pedestrian bridge without set visiting hours.
Crossing the bridge is free.
Old Town Hall and Astronomical Clock
Historic interiors, the famous clock and a panoramic tower.
Founded in the 14th century, the Old Town Hall and its astronomical clock are among Prague's best-known landmarks. The tower offers panoramic views and the visitor circuit includes historic rooms.
Watching the exterior clock is free; tower and building admission is paid.
Jan–Mar daily 10:00–19:00; Apr–Dec daily 9:00–20:00.
Interior circuit CZK 350; reduced CZK 230; family CZK 750. Lift and guided tours cost extra.
Old Town Bridge Tower
A Gothic gateway overlooking Charles Bridge.
The ceremonial gateway to Charles Bridge is a Gothic monument associated with Charles IV. Approximately 138 steps lead to the viewing gallery.
The bridge entrance is free; the tower viewing gallery is paid. Step-free access is limited.
Adults CZK 250; reduced CZK 170; family CZK 500.
Klementinum: Astronomical Tower and Baroque Library
A magnificent library and tower in a Baroque complex.
Join an organised tour to see the monumental library hall and climb the astronomical tower above the historic centre. Tour capacity is limited.
The library is viewed under the tour's rules, not as an open reading room. Advance e-tickets are recommended.
Usually daily 9:00–20:00 within scheduled tours.
Adults CZK 380; reduced CZK 230; family CZK 810.
Josefov: Jewish Museum and Synagogues
Historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery.
The Jewish Museum comprises several sites in Prague's former Jewish quarter. A combined ticket includes historic synagogues and the cemetery, offering a culturally and historically significant visit.
Closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. The Old-New Synagogue may have different hours, particularly on Friday.
1 Sep–17 Oct 2026 9:00–18:00; 18 Oct–31 Dec 2026 9:00–16:30. Closed Saturdays and selected holidays.
Prague Jewish Town circuit: adults CZK 600; students under 26 CZK 400; children 6–15 CZK 200.
Petřín Lookout Tower
A hilltop panorama over the whole city.
The steel tower stands in Petřín's gardens and offers striking views of Prague. Combine the visit with a walk through the greenery and nearby gardens.
Expect stairs. Lift use costs extra; check current availability.
Oct approximately daily 9:00–18:00; Jan–Mar and Nov–Dec 10:00–18:00; other months according to the official website.
Adults CZK 250; reduced CZK 170; family CZK 500; lift extra.
Vyšehrad
Ancient walls, legends and peaceful river views.
The historic fortified site includes parks, the Romanesque Rotunda of St Martin, the Basilica of St Peter and St Paul and Slavín Cemetery. A quieter walk with beautiful views.
The park is freely accessible. Casemates, exhibitions and guided tours charge separately.
Park grounds open year-round; information centre usually 10:00–12:00 and 13:00–18:00.
Public paths free; selected buildings charge according to the programme.
National Museum
History and natural sciences beside Wenceslas Square.
The Historical and New Buildings form one visitor complex. Exhibitions cover history and natural sciences, making the museum a good rainy-day choice.
The Museum Complex ticket does not include some separate exhibitions or the Children's Museum.
Museum Complex: adults CZK 360; reduced CZK 260; accompanied children under 15 free.
National Technical Museum
Transport, inventions and the history of technology.
The museum on Letná explores transport, industry and technological development. Its extensive exhibitions appeal to families and visitors interested in technology and design.
The ore and coal mine exhibition has a separate supplementary admission arrangement.
Closed Monday; usually other days 9:00–18:00. Check exceptions.
Main building: adults CZK 330; reduced CZK 200; children 6–15 CZK 80; family CZK 680.
Prague Zoo
A full day of animals and outdoor exploration in Troja.
Prague Zoo has many exhibits across a large natural outdoor site. Allow several hours and expect hilly terrain.
Some pavilions and entrances close earlier. October closing changes when daylight-saving time ends.
Oct 9:00–17:00, then until 16:00 after the clocks change; Nov–Feb 9:00–16:00; other months seasonal.
At the gate: adults CZK 330; children 3–15 CZK 250; family (2 adults and up to 4 children) CZK 1,000. Online tickets are cheaper.
Prague Botanical Garden, Troja
Outdoor gardens, Fata Morgana greenhouse and a vineyard.
Explore varied outdoor plant collections and a tropical greenhouse. The garden's highlights change with the seasons and exhibitions.
The Fata Morgana greenhouse closes on Monday although the outdoor gardens remain open.
Outdoor gardens Mar–Oct daily 9:00–19:00; Nov–Feb 9:00–16:00. Fata Morgana Tue–Sun.
At the gate: adults CZK 180; children 3–15 CZK 120; family CZK 540. Online CZK 150 / 100 / 450.
Municipal House
Art Nouveau splendour beside the Powder Tower.
One of Prague's finest Art Nouveau buildings has richly decorated interiors. Visit the café or take a guided tour of the ceremonial rooms.
Tours and concerts have their own schedules; ticket office hours do not describe all interior spaces.
Ticket office daily 10:00–19:00; tours according to the schedule.
Guided tour CZK 320; reduced CZK 270; family CZK 660.
Wallenstein Garden
Baroque geometry, peacocks and a grand sala terrena.
One of Malá Strana's most beautiful historic gardens. Carefully framed views, an artificial grotto wall and peacocks invite a short visit.
The garden is outside its main visiting season in winter. Check the specific entrance gate.
Apr–Oct Mon–Fri 7:00–19:00; Sat–Sun 9:00–19:00.
Free admission.
Prague Castle Gardens
Garden terraces, fountains and views towards the centre.
The Royal Garden and accessible southern gardens combine Renaissance, Baroque and later landscape design. A pleasant stop during a castle visit.
Hartig Garden is inaccessible. Other gardens are seasonal and may close exceptionally.
Accessible gardens are free.
Žižkov Television Tower
A modern viewpoint high above Prague.
Žižkov's 216-metre landmark has viewing areas well above the city's rooftops. David Černý's well-known baby sculptures climb its structure.
The observation deck and restaurant are separate operations; event hours may differ.
Daily 9:00–24:00 according to Prague City Tourism.
Observation deck CZK 350; reduced CZK 250; family CZK 750.
Palace Gardens below Prague Castle
Historic terraces and romantic corners on the southern slope.
Several connected palace gardens offer architecture, staircases and viewpoints for a quieter outing away from the main crowds.
Enter from Valdštejnská Street. Direct access to Prague Castle may be closed. Closed during adverse weather.
Apr and Oct daily 10:00–18:00; May–Sep daily 10:00–19:00; seasonal.
Adults CZK 180; reduced CZK 140.
Letná Park
A leafy park with a panorama of Prague's bridges.
Popular Letná Park offers long walking paths, places to rest and views across the Vltava to the historic centre. Combine it with the National Technical Museum.
Restaurants, attractions and the historic carousel have separate operating rules.
Freely accessible public park.
Free park admission.
Dancing House and Gallery
Distinctive modern architecture beside the Vltava.
Designed by Vlado Milunić and Frank Gehry, the Dancing House is one of Prague's best-known modern buildings. Admire its unusual forms outside or visit an exhibition inside.
Photograph the exterior from the riverside without a ticket. Gallery and possible viewpoint access have separate rules.
Gallery daily 9:00–20:00.
Exterior free; gallery CZK 230; reduced CZK 185; family CZK 600.
